title: When Insight Is Not Enough: What’s New in SAP Customer Experience Q2 2026
summary: SAP CX Q2 2026 innovations help shift AI insights to execution, connecting marketing, sales, service, commerce for scalable CX.
body_text: AI has made it easier than ever to identify the next best action. Yet for many organizations, executing those actions consistently across teams, channels, and systems remains the greater challenge. Harmonize your CRM and CX with a single autonomous system Learn how As customer journeys become more connected and complex, gaps in execution can lead to inconsistent experiences, slower response times, and missed opportunities. The next frontier of customer experience is not generating more insights, but turning insight into coordinated action at scale. This latest release of the SAP Customer Experience solution portfolio helps organizations strengthen that foundation by connecting workflows across marketing, commerce, sales, and service—enabling more consistent, scalable execution across every customer interaction. Explore the highlights of the Q2 2026 release. For full sub-solution details, see our recaps for the SAP Commerce Cloud , SAP Sales Cloud , SAP Service Cloud , SAP Enterprise Service Management , and SAP Engagement Cloud solutions. Turning customer intent into action Customer interactions are becoming more conversational, connected, and immediate across channels and touchpoints. At the same time, organizations need faster access to information and simpler ways to take action—whether engaging customers, managing campaigns, or responding to changing business needs. Conversational AI shopping through a model context protocol (MCP) server : Enable secure integration between SAP Commerce Cloud and AI agents that can guide or act on behalf of customers. AI assistants can query real-time product information, provide inventory updates, manage shopping carts, and complete transactions directly within chat or voice interfaces—creating more intelligent, conversational buying experiences beyond the traditional storefront. Conversational AI shopping through an MCP server Joule in SAP Engagement Cloud (SAP Early Adopter Care): Bring SAP’s conversational AI directly into campaign workflows. Teams can ask product or campaign questions in natural language and get accurate answers without searching across multiple systems. They can also duplicate successful campaigns without starting from scratch, freeing more time for strategic thinking, creativity, and customer engagement. Joule with SAP Engagement Cloud Rich communication services (RCS) in SAP Engagement Cloud : Engage customers with rich, interactive messages supported by Google and featuring media, carousels, and action buttons within native mobile messaging experiences. Branded, verified messages help build trust and guide customers smoothly from discovery to purchase without requiring an additional application. RCS chat integration Scaling personalized engagement Recognizing customer intent is only the beginning. As engagement channels expand, marketing teams need to respond quickly while delivering relevant, personalized experiences at scale. This requires frictionless campaign execution, timely insights, and the ability to tailor every interaction to each customer’s needs and preferences. AI-assisted content composer (pilot): Generate high-quality, on-brand campaign content in SAP Engagement Cloud . Using Gemini models informed by audience, product, and campaign context, teams can quickly create and refine content variations so they can launch personalized campaigns faster and spend less time on manual content creation. AI-assisted content composer Embedded audience builder : Enable marketers to access and activate rich data from SAP Customer Data Platform directly within SAP Engagement Cloud. With this capability, they can build advanced segments themselves without switching systems or waiting on data analysts. The precision and relevancy of omnichannel campaigns can be improved by combining behavioral, transactional, account, and profile data with operational data across the business. Audience builder in SAP Engagement Cloud Enabling consistent sales execution at scale Success depends on turning insight into disciplined, repeatable actions that drive predictable revenue outcomes. As sales environments grow more complex, even small inconsistencies in data, priorities, or execution can undermine forecasts and cause opportunities to slip away. Acting with greater consistency and confidence calls for stronger data integrity, aligned behaviors, and clearer guidance. Agentic opportunity summary overview : Give sales teams the tools they need to quickly assess deal health. This capability in SAP Sales Cloud aggregates engagement signals, activity levels, and progress indicators into a real-time view, allowing teams to identify risks early, prioritize effectively, and maintain deal momentum. SAP Sales Cloud, field sales add-on : Optimize sales velocity and help ensure the right product placement with retail execution enabled by intelligent, AI-enhanced processes that maximize revenue. Teams can improve visit planning and execution, harness insights to improve sales performance, and optimize interactions. For consumer products companies, this helps drive shelf availability, promotion compliance, and merchandising effectiveness across retail locations. Field teams gain greater visibility into store-level execution, enabling more consistent brand presence and stronger sell-through performance. SAP Sales Cloud, field sales add-on SAP Incentive Management : Improve sales team effectiveness by using the SAP Incentive Management solution, which is part of sales performance management solutions. It helps drive profitable behaviors that increase revenue and support business growth while providing real-time performance insights, dispute management, and motivating rewards. Teams can use flexible tools to streamline incentive compensation and quickly design, test, and launch sales plans. AI-supported recommendations are also available to guide organizations in optimizing plans, maximizing outcomes, and uncovering actionable insights. SAP Incentive Management Consumer Products Intelligence (SAP Early Adopter Care program): Enable consumer product companies to turn the enormous amount of sales and trade data they generate into better decisions. It uses analytics and AI to help improve trade spend performance, increase sales revenue and margins, and reduce manual effort. Standardizing service execution across the enterprise Service teams are increasingly expected to deliver faster, more reliable support while managing growing complexity across channels and requests. Achieving this objective requires simplifying how services are accessed and helping ensure consistent processes across the organization. Self-service catalog: Allow employees to quickly find what they need without understanding backend processes. Through this guided, intuitive catalog for SAP Enterprise Service Management, requests are automatically routed with the right context, reducing delays and improving resolution times. Self-service catalog Content package framework : Leverage the framework for SAP Enterprise Service Management to deliver rapid, scalable value across lines of business. Prebuilt, reusable configurations for case types, workflows, and catalogs help organizations deploy services more quickly while simplifying implementation across the business. With this approach, organizations can eliminate complexity, empower partners, and speed adoption. Content packages for HR service delivery will be coming soon. Email editor in SAP Service Cloud and SAP Enterprise Service Management : Compose, edit, and manage customer communications more efficiently while maintaining high-quality service interactions. The modern, user-friendly email editor is built for an AI-first world. Email editor in SAP Service Cloud Creation of sales objects from customer hub: Let agents fully manage leads, opportunities, appointments, and sales orders directly from the service agent workspace of SAP Service Cloud. This capability helps turn each customer interaction into an opportunity to deliver more value. Creation of new opportunity in Agent Desktop Accelerating connected order management Turning insight into action requires connected systems that can adapt as the business evolves. As organizations expand order channels, fulfillment networks, and technology landscapes, they need integration and order management that can keep pace so teams can respond faster to change. Flow connector: Enables smooth data flow between the SAP Order Management Services solution, other SAP solutions, and third-party products. This predefined capability allows business users to configure custom business flows and integrations with minimal IT involvement, creating connected order management processes across the enterprise. Flow connector in SAP Order Management Services Execution at scale: the next customer experience advantage As AI becomes embedded in daily operations, the differentiator shifts from insight generation to execution. Our recently announced strategic partnerships with Parloa and Google Cloud help extend this execution-first approach by connecting AI-powered service, commerce, and engagement experiences directly to operational systems and business data. As a result, organizations can move from isolated interactions and insights to coordinated actions that drive faster resolutions, better customer experiences, and greater business impact. title: Robotics in Automotive Manufacturing with Wipro GenAI Agents
summary: Enabling Robust Long-Horizon Intelligence in Automotive Manufacturing.
body_text: Overview Automotive manufacturing increasingly depends on long-horizon workflows where fleets of robots must coordinate across extended, interdependent production sequences. Traditional automation and centralised AI systems struggle to adapt at this scale, often leading to coordination gaps, higher downtime, and rising operational costs. This whitepaper presents a curriculum-guided, hierarchical multi-agent AI framework that combines vision-language models, local decision agents, and a selectively invoked large language model (LLM) oracle . By distributing intelligence across the robotic fleet while retaining global oversight, the approach enables adaptive coordination, uncertainty-aware decision-making, and scalable autonomy on the factory floor. Key Highlights: Multi-Agent Architecture in Automotive Manufacturing Explores the challenges of long-horizon robotic coordination in automotive manufacturing Introduces a distributed, multi-agent architecture that balances local autonomy with global reasoning Demonstrates how vision-language models (VLMs) support flexible perception and task execution Explains the role of confidence calibration using negative log likelihood (NLL) for safe autonomy Outlines a curriculum-guided reinforcement learning approach for progressive skill acquisition Connects architectural choices to manufacturing outcomes such as reduced downtime, improved quality consistency, and scalable deployment Who should read this Manufacturing and operations leaders CTO, CIO, and engineering leaders driving intelligent automation Robotics and AI architects designing scalable factory systems Digital manufacturing and Industry 4.0 teams

title: The Cognitive Campus Blueprint for Enterprise Networking
summary: Demands of AI and cloud networking push data center infrastructure to its limits, operators need networks that are high-performing and extremely reliable.
body_text: The modern enterprise is navigating a profound transformation. The shift to the 'all wireless office' and 'coffee shop type networking', fueled by Wi-Fi 7, AI/ML at the edge, and an explosion in IoT and user devices, has made the network business critical for every enterprise and industry, making network reliability the paramount measure of infrastructure success. Managing disparate domains through siloed operations is unsustainable, escalating complexity directly into operational risk and uncontrolled OpEx. Our strategy at Arista is to confront this complexity head-on by delivering a consistent operational model that spans every domain in the enterprise, establishing a truly Cognitive Campus that addresses the full spectrum of enterprise use cases. Always-On Network: Ensuring continuous service and mission-critical resilience. Zero Touch Operations: Driving network management toward total autonomy and OpEx reduction through intelligent automation. Zero Trust Security: Implementing deep segmentation and strong policy enforcement across all users, devices, and domains. Today we are announcing three critical innovations to advance the next generation of campus networking: 1. Solving Large Scale Campus Mobility with Arista VESPA Campus mobility demands massive scale, but legacy controller designs are breaking under the pressure of extreme user density. This results in unacceptable user experience and high operational risk, directly challenging the always-on network pillar. Arista VESPA is the architectural imperative, applying high-scale data center principles like EVPN to campus network design. It fundamentally breaks the controller dependency, enabling a single, massive roaming domain supporting over 500,000 clients with high resiliency and fast failover. The business value is clear: risk mitigation, operational control (reducing proprietary hardware burden, simplifying network design), and future proofing. Arista VESPA enables design of a single mobility domain across a massive scale campus network 2. AI Ops with AVA Expansion and Agentic AI, Your New Network Assistant To realize zero touch operations, we are expanding the AVA Ⓡ framework with a robust platform approach to Agentic AI. This intelligence is powered by unified data from NetDL Ⓡ (Network Data Lake) and operated consistently via our common OS (Arista EOS Ⓡ ). This platform enables multi-domain event correlation and conversational troubleshooting, fundamentally reducing Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), driving down OpEx, and minimizing human error. Arista AI for Networking Stack 3. Ubiquitous Consistency for Mission-Critical Industrial Edge Deployments To maintain always-on network resilience and zero trust security across the enterprise, policy consistency must extend to the harshest environments. We are introducing two new ruggedized switches (IP50 Din Rail and IP30 1RU) supporting multi-gig and high-power 90W PoE. This ensures the single-OS operational model and security enforcement are consistently applied to industrial, outdoor, and challenging remote locations, eliminating the traditional operational gap at the edge. The Road Ahead: A Unified Vision for the Cognitive Enterprise With these three innovations, Arista VESPA addressing scale, AVA driving automation, and ruggedized platforms extending consistency, we are delivering the next generation of campus networking. This unified approach mitigates complexity, controls costs, and allows our customers to focus on true innovation, not infrastructure management. Welcome to the 2026 era of Cognitive Campus networking! References: Press Release Video Campus White Paper AVA White Paper Webinar

title: Cómo la inteligencia artificial está impactando el empleo y transformando el mercado laboral global
summary: La inteligencia artificial está transformando el empleo, impulsando el reskilling y redefiniendo el talento. Analizamos su impacto.
body_text: Aunque el concepto de inteligencia artificial se ha popularizado especialmente durante el último año, se trata de una tecnología que lleva tiempo presente en nuestro entorno. Diversos estudios apuntan a que, durante la próxima década, una parte significativa de los empleos experimentará cambios relevantes en las tareas y competencias asociadas. Más que una sustitución generalizada de puestos de trabajo, la IA está impulsando una evolución de los roles profesionales, dando lugar a nuevas especializaciones y transformando la forma en que se desarrollan muchas funciones. Este contexto exigirá procesos continuos de reskilling y upskilling, así como una elevada capacidad de adaptación por parte de los profesionales y las organizaciones. La formación permanente y el aprendizaje continuo serán factores clave para aprovechar las oportunidades que ofrece esta nueva realidad tecnológica. Debemos afrontar este cambio con una visión abierta, tanto a nivel individual como organizativo. La inteligencia artificial no sustituye de forma generalizada a las personas, sino que automatiza determinadas tareas y complementa las capacidades humanas. Utilizada de forma adecuada, permite aumentar la productividad, mejorar la toma de decisiones y dedicar más tiempo a actividades de mayor valor añadido. Retos de la inteligencia artificial en el empleo: adaptación, formación y reconversión del talento La evolución de la inteligencia artificial plantea importantes desafíos relacionados con las competencias profesionales, la actualización de conocimientos y la capacidad de adaptación a entornos cada vez más dinámicos. Los principales retos pueden agruparse en dos grandes ámbitos: Agilidad de adaptación y redefinición de funciones. Formación y capacitación continua. Agilidad de adaptación y redefinición de funciones La IA impulsará una transformación constante de los entornos de trabajo, lo que requerirá revisar y redefinir periódicamente procesos, responsabilidades y competencias profesionales. A medida que evolucionen las tecnologías, también evolucionarán las habilidades necesarias para aprovecharlas de manera efectiva. La capacidad de adaptación se convertirá en una competencia estratégica tanto para los profesionales como para las organizaciones, que deberán integrar nuevas herramientas y modelos de trabajo de forma ágil y eficiente. Formación y capacitación continua La actualización permanente de conocimientos será un elemento fundamental para garantizar que los profesionales puedan desenvolverse en un entorno cada vez más digitalizado. Las empresas tendrán además el reto de facilitar el acceso a la formación y a las herramientas necesarias para que esta transformación sea inclusiva, permitiendo que todos los colectivos puedan beneficiarse de las oportunidades que genera la inteligencia artificial. Cómo impulsa Telefónica el acceso a la inteligencia artificial y el desarrollo del talento digital Telefónica mantiene un firme compromiso con el desarrollo de una digitalización inclusiva, facilitando el acceso a la tecnología y al conocimiento digital tanto para ciudadanos como para empresas. Su propósito de hacer nuestro mundo más humano conectando la vida de las personas se traduce en iniciativas orientadas a impulsar la capacitación digital, reducir brechas de acceso y promover una adopción responsable de la inteligencia artificial. A través de Fundación Telefónica, la compañía desarrolla programas destinados a mejorar la empleabilidad, fomentar las competencias digitales y reducir la brecha digital entre distintos colectivos. Entre otras iniciativas, durante el Día Internacional del Voluntariado Telefónica, empleados de la compañía imparten talleres sobre aplicaciones prácticas de la IA para la búsqueda de empleo y actividades de autonomía digital dirigidas a personas mayores, ayudándoles a desenvolverse con mayor confianza en entornos digitales y a reforzar su ciberseguridad. Asimismo, Telefónica pone a disposición del tejido empresarial su experiencia en transformación digital mediante soluciones y servicios que facilitan la adopción de tecnologías de inteligencia artificial. Gracias a sus capacidades en conectividad, cloud, ciberseguridad, datos e inteligencia artificial, la compañía acompaña a las organizaciones en la integración de estas tecnologías, adaptándolas a las necesidades específicas de cada sector y contribuyendo a generar modelos de negocio más innovadores, eficientes y competitivos. Impacto de la inteligencia artificial en la calidad del empleo y la confianza profesional La inteligencia artificial está contribuyendo a transformar la forma de trabajar y puede tener un impacto positivo tanto en la calidad del empleo como en el desarrollo profesional. Su capacidad para automatizar tareas rutinarias permite a los profesionales dedicar más tiempo a actividades estratégicas, creativas y de mayor valor añadido. Al mismo tiempo, el acceso generalizado a herramientas de IA está ampliando las posibilidades de aprendizaje, productividad y generación de conocimiento, facilitando que más personas puedan desarrollar nuevas capacidades y mejorar su desempeño profesional. Este escenario también plantea la necesidad de fomentar un uso responsable y transparente de estas tecnologías. La confianza profesional seguirá apoyándose en aspectos como la experiencia, el pensamiento crítico, el criterio humano y la capacidad para interpretar y validar la información generada por los sistemas de IA. En este sentido, la inteligencia artificial debe entenderse como una herramienta de apoyo que complementa las capacidades humanas y contribuye a potenciar el talento. Tendencias clave de la inteligencia artificial en el empleo y cómo deben prepararse empresas y profesionales Una de las tendencias más relevantes será el fortalecimiento de los modelos de gobernanza, seguridad y gestión de los datos. A medida que la IA se integre de forma más profunda en los procesos empresariales, será imprescindible contar con marcos claros de uso, supervisión y control que garanticen un desarrollo responsable, ético y seguro de estas tecnologías. Otra tendencia estará relacionada con la evolución de las competencias profesionales. Tanto las empresas como los trabajadores deberán impulsar una transformación continua de habilidades, combinando conocimientos tecnológicos con capacidades humanas como el pensamiento crítico, la creatividad, la resolución de problemas y la colaboración. La preparación para este nuevo escenario requerirá invertir en formación, fomentar culturas de aprendizaje continuo y promover entornos laborales en los que las personas y la tecnología trabajen de forma complementaria para generar mayor valor. En este contexto de transformación del empleo, Telefónica refuerza su compromiso de convertirse en la mejor vía de acceso de los ciudadanos a las tecnologías digitales, impulsando iniciativas que combinan innovación, desarrollo del talento y acceso inclusivo a la tecnología. Gracias a sus capacidades tecnológicas, su liderazgo en conectividad, ciberseguridad, cloud, datos e inteligencia artificial, y su apuesta por la formación continua, la compañía contribuye a que personas y empresas aprovechen las oportunidades de la digitalización, construyendo un mercado laboral más preparado, competitivo y alineado con los desafíos de la economía digital.safíos de la economía digital.

title: Syrona Health | News | Syrona Health and Perci Health develop cancer care solution for insurers and employers
body_text: Digital health platform Syrona Health and Perci Health have joined forces to offer a cancer care solution for insurers and employers. Syrona Health offers gender-inclusive healthcare services for different life stages, while Perci Health is a virtual cancer survivorship clinic. The partnership aims to provide a holistic approach to cancer care, offering support at every stage of a patient’s journey. By combining Syrona’s cancer screening with Perci’s personalised prevention and post-diagnosis rehabilitation programmes, the partnership aims to tackle the financial and productivity challenges posed by cancer, supporting patients through every phase – from early detection to long-term recovery. It also aims to improve patient outcomes, increase workplace productivity, and cut absenteeism-related costs for employers. The patient-centred solution combines advanced cancer screening, early detection, and ongoing post-diagnosis support, helping insurers and employers manage the full spectrum of cancer care— from prevention to rehabilitation. Anya Roy, co-founder of Syrona Health, said: “Our partnership with Perci is a game-changer for cancer care. “By combining Syrona’s cancer screening solutions with Perci’s network of highly skilled cancer specialists, we’re creating a seamless, patient-centred journey. “A cancer diagnosis is overwhelming enough without the added stress of navigating a complex healthcare system.” Kelly McCabe, co-founder and CEO of Perci Health, said: “Cancer survivors are often underserved, facing lasting challenges that continue well beyond their diagnosis. “Our partnership with Syrona allows us to deliver personalised, multidisciplinary care to more patients, while helping employers and insurers address the growing costs of cancer care.” Morgan Fitzsimons, co-founder and chief experience officer of Perci Health, said: “At Perci, we’re passionate about using digital innovation to bridge the gaps in healthcare, particularly for underserved groups. “This partnership with Syrona allows us to extend high-quality, personalised cancer care to those who are often left with nowhere to turn. “Together, we’re making sure that technology not only improves access to care but also enhances the quality of support for those who need it most.” Chantelle Bell, co-founder of Syrona Health, said: “This partnership combines Syrona’s technological innovation with Perci’s deep understanding of cancer care. “We’re set to transform the cancer care landscape, making it more accessible, personalised, and ultimately, more human.”

title: The Shutdown Ritual: How to Actually Stop Working at the End of the Day - Sunsama Blog
summary: Learn how to build a shutdown ritual that actually ends your workday. A step-by-step guide to closing mental loops, planning tomorrow, and reclaiming your evenings.
body_text: You finished your last meeting at 5:30. It's now 8:45, and you're still "just checking one more thing" while dinner gets cold. Your laptop sits open on the kitchen counter. Your mind keeps looping back to that email you didn't send, that task you might have forgotten, that project that feels perpetually unfinished. This isn't a time management problem. It's a shutdown ritual problem — or rather, the absence of one. Without a clear ending to your workday, work doesn't actually end. It just fades into a gray zone where you're never fully working and never fully resting. The result? You're exhausted but unproductive, present but distracted, technically "off" but mentally still on. This post will show you exactly how to build a shutdown ritual that creates a clean break between work and life — not as a productivity hack, but as an act of professional self-respect. Why Your Brain Can't Stop Working (Even When You Want It To) The reason you can't stop thinking about work isn't a character flaw. It's a well-documented cognitive phenomenon that explains why willpower alone won't save you. The Zeigarnik Effect Is Running the Show In the 1920s, psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik noticed something peculiar: waiters could remember complex orders perfectly — until the moment the bill was paid. Then the details vanished. Her research revealed that incomplete tasks create a kind of mental tension. Your brain keeps them active, running in the background like browser tabs you can't close. This is why you lie awake thinking about tomorrow's presentation. The task is open. Your brain is trying to hold it. Open Loops Drain Your Mental Battery Every unfinished task, unanswered question, or vague commitment takes up cognitive real estate. Cal Newport calls this "attention residue" — the mental fragments that linger after you switch contexts. Without a ritual to close these loops, you carry dozens of them into your evening. The fix isn't to finish everything. That's impossible. The fix is to convince your brain that everything is captured, planned, and safely stored somewhere outside your head. The Myth of the Seamless Day Modern knowledge work has erased the natural boundaries that once separated work from rest. Factory workers heard a whistle. Farmers watched the sun set. You? You have a laptop that travels everywhere and notifications that never sleep. Without physical boundaries, you need psychological ones . A shutdown ritual creates an artificial edge to your day — a clear signal that work is complete, even when work itself is never truly "done." The Anatomy of an Effective Shutdown Ritual Not all shutdown rituals are equal. Some are too flimsy to create real closure. Others are so elaborate they become another task you dread. Here's what actually works. The Three Functions Every Ritual Must Serve An effective shutdown ritual accomplishes three things: Capture : Get everything out of your head and into a trusted system Review : Confirm that nothing urgent is falling through the cracks Plan : Make a concrete decision about tomorrow so your brain can let go Skip any of these, and your mind will keep spinning. Capture without review leaves you anxious about what you might have missed. Review without planning leaves tomorrow feeling uncertain. Planning without capture means you're building on an incomplete foundation. The Ideal Length: 10-15 Minutes Your shutdown ritual should be short enough to actually do and long enough to be meaningful. Ten to fifteen minutes hits the sweet spot. Anything shorter tends to feel rushed and incomplete. Anything longer starts to feel like unpaid overtime. The goal is a ritual you'll actually perform, especially on the days when you're exhausted and just want to close your laptop and walk away. Those are precisely the days when you need it most. Consistency Over Intensity A mediocre ritual performed daily beats a perfect ritual performed occasionally. Your brain learns to associate the ritual with "work is ending." Over time, the ritual itself becomes the trigger for mental disengagement. This is why the specific steps matter less than the consistency. Pick a sequence you can sustain, then protect it. A Step-by-Step Shutdown Ritual You Can Use Tonight Here's a concrete ritual you can implement immediately. Adapt it to your context, but don't skip the core elements. Step 1: Process Your Inbox to Zero (5 Minutes) This doesn't mean responding to every email. It means making a decision about every email. Delete, delegate, defer, or do — but don't leave messages sitting in limbo. For each message, ask: "Does this require action? If so, when?" Move actionable items to your task list with a specific date. Archive everything else. The goal is an empty inbox, not an empty to-do list. Pro Tip: Set a timer for this step. Without a constraint, inbox processing expands to fill all available time. Five minutes forces quick decisions. Step 2: Review Today's Unfinished Tasks (3 Minutes) Look at what you planned to do today. For each unfinished item, make one of three choices: Reschedule : Move it to a specific future date Delegate : Assign it to someone else Delete : Acknowledge it's not happening and remove it The worst option is leaving tasks floating in today's list. They'll haunt you. Make a decision, even if the decision is "not this week." Try it in Sunsama: Sunsama's daily shutdown flow walks you through each incomplete task, prompting you to reschedule or remove it. No orphaned tasks, no lingering guilt. Step 3: Scan Tomorrow's Calendar (2 Minutes) Open tomorrow's calendar. Look for meetings that require preparation. Note any early commitments that affect your morning routine. Identify potential conflicts or gaps. You're not planning tomorrow in detail — you're reducing surprise. When you know what's coming, your brain relaxes its vigilance. Step 4: Choose Tomorrow's Priority Tasks (3 Minutes) Select one to three tasks that would make tomorrow feel successful. Not everything you might do. Not everything you could do. Just the tasks that matter most. Write them down somewhere you'll see them in the morning. This primes your brain for focused work and eliminates the "what should I work on?" decision fatigue that often derails mornings. Try it in Sunsama: Sunsama's daily planning pulls in tasks from your various tools and prompts you to timeblock them onto your calendar. Tomorrow's priorities become concrete commitments, not vague intentions. Step 5: Say the Shutdown Phrase (10 Seconds) This sounds silly. Do it anyway. Cal Newport recommends a verbal cue to signal completion: "Shutdown complete." Others use "Schedule closed" or "Done for today." The specific words don't matter. What matters is the auditory and kinesthetic signal that work is finished. Say it out loud. Close your laptop. Walk away. The Most Common Shutdown Mistakes (And How to Avoid Them) Even well-intentioned rituals fail. Here's what derails most people. Treating It as Optional The shutdown ritual is most valuable on your hardest days — when you're behind, overwhelmed, or anxious about tomorrow. Those are exactly the days you'll want to skip it. Treat the ritual as non-negotiable. It's not a reward for finishing everything. It's how you finish, period. Checking Email After Shutdown Nothing sabotages a shutdown faster than "one quick peek" at your inbox. You'll see something that creates anxiety or demands response, and suddenly you're back in work mode. Build a hard rule: after shutdown, email is closed. If this feels impossible, ask yourself what emergency your inbox will contain that truly can't wait until morning. The answer is almost always "nothing." Confusing Shutdown With Planning Your shutdown ritual captures and clarifies. Your morning planning session prioritizes and executes. These are different activities with different purposes. If you find yourself spending 30 minutes each evening in detailed planning, you've merged two rituals. Keep shutdown focused on closure. Save deep planning for when you're fresh. Skipping the Physical Transition Mental rituals work better with physical anchors. Close the laptop lid. Stand up. Leave the room where you work. Change clothes. Take a short walk. Your brain evolved to understand physical transitions. Give it one. Why "Finish Everything" Is the Wrong Goal Here's where conventional productivity advice gets it wrong: it implies that the shutdown ritual is about completion. Finish your tasks, then shut down. Clear your inbox, then relax. This framing is backward. You Will Never Be "Done" Knowledge work has no natural endpoint. There's always another email, another improvement, another opportunity. If shutdown depends on completion, you'll never shut down. The ritual isn't about finishing work. It's about finishing your engagement with work — even while tasks remain incomplete. Incompleteness Is Normal, Not Failure That open loop on your task list? It's not evidence of personal failure. It's evidence that you're doing ambitious work with finite time. The most productive professionals consistently have more ideas than hours. Your shutdown ritual is an act of acceptance: you did what you could with today. Tomorrow will come with its own time and energy. For now, you're released. Rest Is Productive A proper shutdown enables genuine recovery. And genuine recovery — not just distracted half-rest — is what allows you to return tomorrow with focus and energy. When you skip the shutdown ritual and spend your evening in low-grade work anxiety, you're borrowing from tomorrow's productivity to fund today's illusion of availability. It's a bad trade. How to Handle the Hardest Shutdown Scenarios Some situations make shutdown genuinely difficult. Here's how to adapt. When You're Behind on a Deadline The temptation to push through is strong. Before you skip your shutdown, ask: "Will another hour tonight produce better work than a fresh hour tomorrow morning?" Usually, the answer is no. Exhausted evening work tends to be slow and error-prone. A proper shutdown plus adequate sleep often nets you more total progress. If you must work late, still perform a modified shutdown when you stop. Even at 10 PM, the ritual helps your brain release. When You're Waiting on Someone Else Open loops that depend on other people feel particularly unresolvable. You can't close them yourself. The fix is to reframe the task. Instead of "Waiting for Sarah's feedback," your task becomes "Follow up with Sarah if no response by Thursday." Now you have a concrete next action on a specific date. The ball is in your court, even while it's also in hers. Pro Tip: Create a "Waiting For" category in your task system. During shutdown, review it briefly. Any items that need a follow-up nudge get scheduled. Everything else can rest. When Anxiety Keeps Intruding Sometimes you complete the ritual and your mind still races. You've captured everything, planned tomorrow, said the phrase — but the worry persists. Keep a small notebook by your bed. When work thoughts intrude, write them down. Don't engage with them; just capture them. Tell your brain: "I heard you. It's recorded. We'll address it tomorrow." Often, the act of writing is enough to release the thought. Try it in Sunsama: If you think of something after shutdown, add it to Sunsama from your phone. It'll appear in tomorrow's planning session, properly captured. Your brain can let go because the system won't forget. How to Make the Ritual Stick: The First Two Weeks Knowing the ritual isn't the same as doing the ritual. Here's how to build the habit. Start With a Trigger Attach your shutdown ritual to something that already happens reliably. "After my last meeting ends." "When my 5 PM alarm goes off." "Before I leave my desk for the day." The trigger should be specific and consistent. "When I feel ready to stop" is too vague to build a habit around. Lower the Bar Initially During the first week, aim for a 5-minute ritual. Capture, quick review, one priority for tomorrow, shutdown phrase. That's it. It's more valuable to do a short ritual daily than to attempt the full version and abandon it by Wednesday. Track Your Streak Mark each successful shutdown on a calendar or habit tracker. The visual chain of completed days creates its own motivation. You won't want to break the streak. After two weeks of daily practice, the ritual will start to feel automatic. That's when you can expand it. Your Shutdown Ritual Starter Checklist Here's a simple framework for tonight: Process inbox to zero (decide, don't necessarily respond) Review today's incomplete tasks — reschedule, delegate, or delete each one Scan tomorrow's calendar for surprises Select 1-3 priority tasks for tomorrow Say your shutdown phrase out loud Close your laptop and leave your workspace Set a recurring reminder for 15 minutes before you want to stop working. When it fires, begin the ritual. No exceptions for the first two weeks. The ritual won't feel natural immediately. That's fine. You're not looking for comfort; you're looking for closure. The comfort comes later, once your brain learns to trust the system. Your work will still be there tomorrow. Your inbox will refill. Your task list will regenerate. That's the nature of meaningful work — it's never finished. But you can be finished for today. The shutdown ritual is how you claim that truth, close the loops, and walk away whole. ‍

title: This is Roark v2
summary: Roark v2 is a ground-up rebuild of our voice-AI testing platform: simulation templates, a new look with dark mode, faster reporting, and self-serve pay-as-you-go pricing.
body_text: Today we're introducing Roark v2. Not a redesign. Not a new logo bolted onto the old product. We rebuilt Roark from the first pixel to the last query. Every screen, every report, every interaction, rebuilt from scratch around one question: what does it actually feel like to test and trust a voice agent in production? The answer is the most significant release in our history. And it is live right now. Watch the Roark v2 launch film Rebuilt from the ground up We didn't refactor Roark. We rebuilt it. The entire application is new. New foundation, new navigation, new defaults, all shaped by a year of watching real teams create agents, run simulations, and chase down failing checks. Metrics are the center of gravity now. The AI assistant is one keystroke away from any page. The left nav is organized around the loop you actually run: Monitor, Measure, Simulate, Build. This is what "rebuilt from scratch" really means. We kept everything you loved, and threw out everything that got in your way. A completely new look Roark v2 is a full rebrand and a full rebuild, at the same time. The new interface is calmer, faster, and easier to read. Information has room to breathe. The controls you need are where you reach for them. And yes, dark mode is here, designed as a first-class experience, so the people who live in Roark at 2am finally have a home that looks the part. Even the docs are rebuilt, rethemed, and rewritten from the ground up at docs.roark.ai . It is the first time the product looks as considered as the work it does. Simulations, built on templates This is the part I am most excited about. Testing a voice agent used to mean building a run from a blank page every time. Not anymore. Simulations in Roark v2 start from templates: pick a preset like Flow adherence, Red teaming, or Conversation quality, set your pass and fail thresholds per metric before the run, and go. The template carries the criteria, so the outcome is graded inline the moment the run finishes. Every new workspace ships with system flows and templates out of the box, so there is something real to run on day one. Starting a simulation run from a template, with Flow adherence, Red teaming, and Conversation quality presets Templates sit on top of a bigger idea we shipped alongside the rebuild: Customer Flows. Design what a customer actually does once, then run it against any agent. Scripted or improv. A scripted variant follows a graph you drew. An improv variant follows a plain-text brief and lets the persona ad-lib. Generate flows with Roark. Paste a transcript, pick a few real calls, or just describe the intent, and the assistant recommends improv vs scripted and builds it for you. Multilingual fan-out. 34 system personas across 17 languages, plus code-switching variants. Attach a flow once, run it once per language. Test flow in one click. Finish a flow and the Test flow button drops you straight into a pre-filled run, agent and variants already attached. And when a run is live, you watch it happen. Live Simulation View opens into a mission-control board with per-call status, elapsed timers, and streaming transcripts, turn by turn, so you can listen in, cut a bad call short, or re-run a single case on the spot. Reporting, rebuilt for speed Reporting was the heart of the old Roark, and it was showing its age. So we tore it down and built it again. The new reporting engine is dramatically faster, and far more useful. Compare up to five checks or metrics across up to five prior runs on a radar you can actually read. Get a column per metric and per check, not just the first three. Tap any check to filter the calls table. There is even a new agent_responsive check, computed on every simulation for free, that catches runs where your agent went silent while the customer was still talking. And load testing now runs ten times the iterations at no extra cost. Reporting is no longer the thing you wait on. It is the thing you move through. Intelligence, everywhere you look The most powerful part of Roark v2 is what it does on its own. Roarky, your on-screen guide and analyst. Ask in plain English, "track how often callers ask about pricing," and Roarky builds the whole chain: it finds or creates the metric, starts a collector so it runs on every new call, and drops a chart on your dashboard. Ask "walk me through running my first simulation" and it drives the navigation, spotlighting each control as it goes. The in-app AI assistant pinned to the right rail AI-detected issues. Recurring failures across your production calls now cluster themselves into stable, Sentry-style issues automatically. No alert rules to configure. The patterns find you. Recurring behavioral failures grouped into stable, AI-detected issues The end-to-end prompt optimizer. After a simulation settles, Roark reads the failing checks, the worst calls, and your current prompt, then proposes targeted edits with anchors and evidence. Fix it, re-run the suite, and get proof it moved. The prompt optimizer suggesting evidence-grounded edits after a simulation run Knowledge bases. Give a judge metric the real rubric and a compliance metric the real policy document, so Roark scores against your source of truth instead of an approximation of it. Confidence in production Testing is half the story. Roark v2 also tells you the truth about what is happening live. Health checks and uptime. Roark now answers the simplest question about your agent: is it answering right now? Pick a cadence, and every monitor renders as a clean status-page card. Health checks page with status cards and 24-hour probe history Deterministic or adaptive, your call. A branching-mode toggle lets one flow either fan out into a simulation per path, or collapse into a single call the agent has to navigate live. Flow editor with the deterministic and adaptive branching-mode toggle Fine-grained PII redaction lets you choose exactly which categories to redact across both audio and transcript. And in-car detection, a new system metric, flags when a caller is in a vehicle, so you understand the real conditions your agents work through. A new plan, and pricing that gets out of the way We rebuilt the business model too, and gave it a new front door. Roark v2 introduces a brand new Pay-as-you-go plan: fully self-serve, usage-based in plain dollars, and free to start. Sign up, run your first simulation, and pay only for what you actually use, with no sales call and no contract. It sits alongside Team and Enterprise, and there is no feature gating between tiers, so you get the whole platform on every plan. This is just the beginning Roark v2 is the platform we always wanted to build. Faster, smarter, and more beautiful than anything we have shipped before, with simulation templates that get you testing in seconds, an intelligence layer that does the tedious work for you, and a testing loop that earns your confidence before launch. It is all live today, and it is free to try. Open Roark, switch on dark mode, and see what the whole thing feels like now. Welcome to Roark v2.

title: Choosing the right IPMS for trademarks: Why risk control needs more than recordkeeping
summary: Discover how connected data, workflows and portfolio visibility help trademark teams identify risk early and make informed decisions.
body_text: Trademark risk is rarely caused by one missed deadline or one incomplete record. More often, it builds when decisions, business context and portfolio activity are disconnected. For trademark leaders, the right IP management system should do more than store information. It should help teams identify risk earlier, manage decisions consistently and make data-driven portfolio decisions that minimize risk and optimize revenue strategies with confidence. In this blog, Jill Clark, Lead Product Consultant at Clarivate and former corporate and law firm trademark paralegal, explores why effective trademark risk control depends on connected data, structured workflows and practical visibility across the portfolio. Drawing on real-world trademark experience, Jill explains how IPfolio helps trademark teams move beyond simple recordkeeping to advanced decision-making that manages risk and optimizes value. Why trademark risk control starts with connected information In my last post , I talked about the difference between information and insight. Trademark teams may have the records and dates they need, and even the reports leadership asks for, but still struggle to answer questions with confidence. Risk control is the next part of that conversation. When I worked in trademark prosecution, risk did not always look dramatic. Sometimes it looked like a renewal notice for a mark tied to a product no longer sold. Sometimes it was an ownership update handled on a single record but never carried over to the rest of the portfolio. Sometimes it was a clearance discussion that happened over email, with the reasoning never tied back to the trademark record. None of those issues may feel urgent in the moment. Across a large portfolio, they add up. They create uncertainty. They make it harder to know what has been reviewed, what still needs action and where the business may be carrying avoidable risk. That is why choosing the right IP management system matters. For trademark teams, an IP Management System (IPMS) should do more than store marks and documents or track important dates. It should help the team see risk earlier, manage decisions consistently and explain what happened later. Trademark risk can hide in plain sight A deadline may be docketed correctly. Outside counsel may send a reminder on time. The record may look complete. But that does not mean the team has the full picture. A trademark portfolio changes constantly. Brands expand. Products are retired. Companies reorganize. Markets shift. New conflicts appear. In-use requirements come due. Renewal decisions need current business input. If the IP management system only stores records, the team still has to build the risk picture manually. That usually means moving back and forth between emails, spreadsheets and docket reports, then trying to confirm the business context before anyone feels confident. IPfolio helps reduce that manual work by bringing more of that context into one place. The trademark record can show more than the mark itself. It can connect to ownership, prosecution activity, key dates, related products, business units, documents, outside counsel updates and portfolio status. That gives the team a clearer view of what needs attention and why. That matters at every level. A paralegal needs to know what needs action. An attorney needs the context behind the legal decision. A manager needs to see workload and open issues. A leader needs confidence that risk is being monitored and not buried in someone’s inbox. Why disconnected trademark decisions create risk Trademark work includes a steady stream of judgment calls. Should the team oppose a similar mark? Should it renew a registration tied to an older product? Should it keep protection in a country where the business has scaled back? Should it clear a new brand in one market but hold off in another? The risk is not only whether the team makes the right decision. It is whether the decision is based on the right information and captured where others can find it later. When decisions live in email threads or separate files, teams lose institutional memory. A new team member may not know why a mark was maintained. A business leader may question renewal spend without seeing the reason behind it. A future clearance review may miss prior concerns because the earlier analysis was never tied to the record. This is where an IPMS needs to support the work around the record. For trademark teams, the system should connect the legal record to the activity and decisions surrounding it. That includes prosecution history, ownership questions, watch activity, renewal decisions and outside counsel input. In IPfolio, that connected structure helps the team avoid treating each trademark as an isolated record. The mark can sit within the broader business and legal context. That makes it easier to see what has happened, what is still open and what may need to be escalated. What practical trademark risk control looks like Good risk control does not mean every risk disappears. It means the team can see, track and explain the risk. That sounds simple, but it is often where systems fall short. A trademark team may need to know which marks have upcoming deadlines that require business input. They may also need to identify registrations tied to inactive products, monitor open conflicts or understand which decisions are waiting on outside counsel, internal review, or budget approval. Those are not merely administrative considerations. They can influence costs, revenue, portfolio strategy, brand reputation and overall legal risk. IPfolio can support this through structured data, workflows and dashboards that surface the work needing attention. Instead of relying on one-off spreadsheets, teams can use current portfolio information to review renewals, monitor open items and prepare for leadership conversations. This becomes even more important for global trademark portfolios. One deadline may be easy to manage. Hundreds or thousands of deadlines across jurisdictions are different. Without reliable context, everything can start to look equally important. With the right IPMS structure, teams can separate routine maintenance from decisions that require review. How IPMS workflows help reduce gaps One of the most practical ways to reduce trademark risk is through better workflows. Trademark work depends on handoffs. A business team may request clearance. An attorney may assess the risk. Outside counsel may file a response. A paralegal may manage the date and supporting documents. Leadership may need to approve the cost or strategy. When those handoffs happen informally, the work may still get done, but the process depends too much on individual follow-up. That creates risk when people are busy, roles change or the portfolio grows. IPfolio can help teams define workflows around these moments. A clearance request can follow a consistent review path. A renewal decision can require business input before action is taken. A watch notice can be reviewed, escalated and documented. A prosecution task can be assigned, tracked and tied back to the correct record. The system does not replace legal and business judgment. Trademark professionals still make the decisions. The value is that the process around those decisions becomes more visible and consistent. How to choose an IPMS with risk control in mind When organizations evaluate an IPMS, risk control should be part of the conversation from the beginning. It is easy to focus on recordkeeping, deadline tracking and reporting. Those matter. But they do not tell the full story. The better question is whether the system helps the team manage the decisions and exceptions that create risk. Can the team see what needs attention without relying on manual follow-up? Can legal records connect to business context? Can workflows reflect how issues are reviewed, escalated and resolved? Can leadership see risk clearly enough to act on it? These questions matter because trademark risk is not controlled by data alone. It is controlled when the right data is connected to the right workflow at the right time. For trademark teams, IPfolio is strongest when it is used for that broader purpose. It brings together structured records, workflow management, reporting and portfolio visibility so teams can move from reacting to issues to managing them with more confidence. The right IPMS should do more than tell a team what it owns. It should help teams spot emerging risks early, understand their potential impact and act with confidence before those risks turn into costly problems or missed opportunities. Manage trademark risk with greater confidence Trademark teams need more than reliable recordkeeping. They need systems that help them connect data, decisions and workflows, so they can manage risk proactively and explain portfolio actions clearly. IPfolio helps trademark teams bring portfolio information, workflow management and reporting visibility together in one IP management system. To learn how Clarivate can help your team improve trademark risk control and make more confident IP decisions, speak to our team at Clarivate.com/DiscoverIPfolio . title: Hyperfine Announces First Patients Enrolled in PRISM PMR to Evaluate the Use of Next-Generation Swoop® System in the Operating Room Setting
summary: Hyperfine launches study to assess Swoop® System use in neurosurgical ORs, advancing accessible brain MRI across care settings.
body_text: With several patients already enrolled in the study, PRISM PMR is designed to evaluate the Swoop® system’s clinical utility in the operating room. Guilford, CT – October 21, 2025 – Hyperfine, Inc. (Nasdaq: HYPR), the groundbreaking health technology company that has redefined brain imaging with the first FDA-cleared AI-powered portable MRI system for the brain—the Swoop® system—today announced plans for clinical use expansion into the operating room environment, advancing its mission to make brain MRI more accessible across a diversity of care settings. The company plans to establish a foothold in the neurosurgical operating setting by launching a new study to build a body of clinical evidence for Swoop® system use in neurosurgical procedures. PRISM PMR (PRe- and post-operatIve Study of iMaging with Portable MR) is designed to further collect data and optimize the Swoop® system’s real-world clinical utility in the operating room. The study will evaluate the pre- and post-procedure use of portable MRI across a diverse range of neurosurgical procedures, including its ability to detect post-operative complications, such as stroke and bleeding, and how it can be best integrated into the surgical workflow to accelerate discharge and recovery. The study has enrolled its first patients and is led by the principal investigator, Dr. Elad Levy, MD, MBA, a globally recognized pioneer in the field of neurovascular disease. It is being conducted over three months at the Atlas Surgery Center in Buffalo, New York. “The operating room is an exciting new setting and use case for the portable MRI market. Having a high-field MRI right in the OR is not practical. The PRISM PMR study and Dr. Levy’s pioneering work illustrates how the Swoop® system can potentially reshape neurosurgical care, bringing valuable clinical insights and workflow benefits,” said Hyperfine President and Chief Executive Officer Maria Sainz. “By enabling neurosurgeons to obtain critical imaging immediately before and after a procedure, the Swoop® system can help improve patient safety, reduce costs, and transform how surgical centers think about imaging infrastructure.” Dr. Levy commented, “MRI is a cornerstone in imaging patients undergoing neurovascular procedures, and having the ability to perform imaging immediately after surgery in the operating room is transformative,” said Dr. Elad Levy, neurosurgeon at Atlas Surgery Center. “Portable brain MRI allows us to confirm results, rule out major complications, and potentially safely discharge patients on the same day. This technology has the potential to redefine surgical workflows and change how we care for patients. It’s also helping us eliminate bottlenecks by shifting appropriate patients to the ambulatory setting, which in turn frees up valuable surgical capacity in the hospital.” In addition to being part of the PRISM PMR study, Dr. Levy recently highlighted the value of having post-operative MRI on a live surgery case at the Congress of Neurological Surgeons, demonstrating the growing clinical interest and relevance of portable brain MRI in a surgical setting. Using the Swoop® system post-procedure allowed Dr. Levy and his team to assess the intracranial environment, rule out complications, and support the possibility of same-day discharge—capabilities traditionally limited to hospitals equipped with large, costly intraoperative MRI systems requiring specialized siting and infrastructure. For more information about the Swoop® system, please visit HyperfineMRI.com . About the Swoop® Portable MRI Systems The Swoop® Portable MR Imaging® Systems are U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared for brain imaging of patients of all ages. They are portable, ultra-low-field magnetic resonance imaging devices for producing images that display the internal structure of the head where full diagnostic examination is not clinically practical. When interpreted by a trained physician, these images provide information that can be useful in determining a diagnosis. About Hyperfine, Inc. Hyperfine, Inc. (Nasdaq: HYPR) is the groundbreaking health technology company that has redefined brain imaging with the Swoop® system—the first FDA-cleared, portable, ultra-low-field, magnetic resonance brain imaging system capable of providing imaging at multiple points of professional care. The mission of Hyperfine, Inc. is to revolutionize patient care globally through transformational, accessible, clinically relevant diagnostic imaging. Founded by Dr. Jonathan Rothberg in a technology-based incubator called 4Catalyzer, Hyperfine, Inc. scientists, engineers, and physicists developed the Swoop® system out of a passion for redefining brain imaging methodology and how clinicians can apply accessible diagnostic imaging to patient care. For more information, visit HyperfineMRI.com . The Hyperfine logo, Swoop, and Portable MR Imaging are registered trademarks of Hyperfine, Inc. The Swoop logo, Optive AI logo, and Optive AI are trademarks of Hyperfine, Inc. title: Nexstar Announces Completion of ATSC 3.0 Transition in Cleveland, Marking Upgrade in Final Major U.S. Market
summary: IRVING, TX – Nexstar Media Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: NXST), today announced the successful launch of ATSC 3.0 (NextGen TV) in the Cleveland, Ohio, television
body_text: IRVING, TX – Nexstar Media Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: NXST), today announced the successful launch of ATSC 3.0 (NextGen TV) in the Cleveland, Ohio, television market, with the next-generation broadcast standard now deployed across all of the top 25 U.S. designated market areas (DMAs). As the largest remaining market yet to deploy ATSC 3.0, Cleveland had been unable to launch due to structural limitations in available broadcast spectrum and station participation. However, following Nexstar’s 2024 acquisition of WBNX-TV, Nexstar contributed the station’s spectrum to the ATSC 3.0 effort, enabling the entire Cleveland market to align the necessary technical and operational resources necessary to move forward. This is a clear example of how strategic industry consolidation can accelerate innovation and deliver meaningful benefits to consumers. The transition makes Cleveland the last large U.S. market to complete deployment of ATSC 3.0, a milestone that effectively establishes nationwide availability of the new broadcast standard in all major markets. ATSC 3.0 technology provides viewers with a significantly enhanced experience, including: Interactive content and enhanced data services, including a terrestrial backup to GPS Superior picture quality, including 4K UHD and HDR capabilities Immersive audio Advanced emergency alerting features “Completing this ATSC 3.0 transition represents a significant milestone in the nationwide transformation of broadcast capabilities and is the first step to bringing a host of benefits to consumers in the Cleveland DMA,” said Brett Jenkins, Nexstar’s Chief Technology & Digital Officer. “NextGen TV service also opens up opportunities for EdgeBeam Wireless, our joint venture, to offer its services to customers looking to take advantage of the benefits of data delivery over a broadcast system for such applications as high-precision positioning, digital signage, and enhancing public safety.” Viewers in the Cleveland market can access NextGen TV broadcasts with a compatible television set or external receiver. Existing ATSC 1.0 services will continue to be available during the transition period to ensure uninterrupted access. ### About Nexstar Media Group: Nexstar Media Group, Inc.
